title: A right exact linear module functor preserving sums is tensoring by its value on the ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $F:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ be a functor on the category of all $R$-modules in a fixed universe containing $R$. Suppose its maps on hom modules are $R$-linear, that it takes every exact sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ to an exact sequence $F(M_1)\to F(M_2)\to F(M_3)\to0$, and that it preserves every direct sum indexed by a set in this universe (the canonical coproduct comparison is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). For $m\in M$ write $u_m:R\to M$ for $r\mapsto rm$. The $R$-bilinear rule $(x,m)\mapsto F(u_m)(x)$ defines a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $\theta_M:F(R)\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M)$, where the tensor product represents $R$-bilinear maps.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), exercise: any right exact R-linear module functor commuting with direct sums is tensoring with an R-module; the canonical map is written explicitly here.

proof.text: Put $N=F(R)$ and $T(M)=N\otimes_R M$. The rule $b_M(x,m)=F(u_m)(x)$ is linear in $x$, because $F(u_m)$ is a module homomorphism. Since $u_{m+m'}=u_m+u_{m'}$ and $u_{rm}=r u_m$, linearity of $F$ on hom modules gives $b_M(x,m+m')=b_M(x,m)+b_M(x,m')$ and $b_M(x,rm)=r b_M(x,m)$. Thus the stated tensor universal property gives the linear map $\theta_M:T(M)\to F(M)$. For $a:M\to M'$, the equality $a u_m=u_{a(m)}$ gives $F(a)\theta_M(x\otimes m)=\theta_{M'}(x\otimes a(m))$. Equality on pure tensors, hence the tensor universal property, proves naturality.

proof.text: For $M=R$, $u_r=r\,\mathrm{id}_R$, so $\theta_R(x\otimes r)=rx$. Its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$: the two composites are identities because $rx\otimes1=x\otimes r$. This verifies the normalization at the rank-one free module without choosing any isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), exercise on right exact linear module functors preserving direct sums (expanded by the worker).

proof.text: For a set $I$ in the fixed universe let $P_I=R^{(I)}$ be finitely supported coefficient families, with basis vectors $e_i$ and coprojections $j_i:R\to P_I$. This is the coproduct: a map out is uniquely prescribed by its values on the $e_i$, by the formula $\sum_i r_i e_i\mapsto\sum_i r_i f(e_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define $\alpha_I:N\otimes_R P_I\to N^{(I)}$ by $\alpha_I(x\otimes\sum_i r_i e_i)=\sum_i\iota_i(r_i x)$. The right side is bilinear, by addition of finite coefficient families and the module laws, so it defines a linear map. Define $\beta_I:N^{(I)}\to N\otimes_R P_I$ by $\beta_I(\sum_i\iota_i(x_i))=\sum_i x_i\otimes e_i$. These maps are inverse: $\alpha_I\beta_I$ fixes each $\iota_i(x)$, while $\beta_I\alpha_I(x\otimes\sum_i r_i e_i)=\sum_i r_i x\otimes e_i=x\otimes\sum_i r_i e_i$. The formulas include $I=\varnothing$, when both sides are zero.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), exercise on right exact linear module functors preserving direct sums (expanded by the worker).

proof.text: The direct-sum comparison $c_I:N^{(I)}\to F(P_I)$ is characterized by $c_I\iota_i=F(j_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $F$. On each summand, $\theta_{P_I}\beta_I\iota_i(x)=\theta_{P_I}(x\otimes e_i)=F(j_i)(x)$, since $u_{e_i}=j_i$. Uniqueness of a map from a direct sum therefore gives $\theta_{P_I}\beta_I=c_I$. Since $\beta_I$ and $c_I$ are isomorphisms, so is $\theta_{P_I}$ for every set $I$ in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), exercise on right exact linear module functors preserving direct sums (expanded by the worker).

proof.text: Given $M$, take $I$ to be its underlying set and let $p:P_I\to M$ send $e_m$ to $m$. This is surjective because $p(e_m)=m$. Let $J$ be the underlying set of $\ker p$, and define $d:P_J\to P_I$ by sending $e_k$ to the element $k\in\ker p\subseteq P_I$. Then $\operatorname{im}d=\ker p$: one inclusion follows from $pd=0$, and the other from $d(e_k)=k$. Thus $P_J\xrightarrow{d}P_I\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ is exact. Both $I$ and $J$ are sets of the original universe, because kernels are subsets and finitely supported families over $R$ remain in that universe.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), exercise on right exact linear module functors preserving direct sums (expanded by the worker).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], applied to $P_J\xrightarrow{d}P_I\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ and the arbitrary module $N=F(R)$, the row $T(P_J)\xrightarrow{T(d)}T(P_I)\xrightarrow{T(p)}T(M)\to0$ is exact. The corresponding row $F(P_J)\xrightarrow{F(d)}F(P_I)\xrightarrow{F(p)}F(M)\to0$ is exact by the given right exactness of $F$. Step 1 supplies the commuting vertical maps $\theta$, and step 4 makes the first two vertical maps isomorphisms. No flatness of $N$ is used.

source.place: Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact; applied to the explicit free presentation in step 5.

proof.text: Surjectivity of $\theta_M$ follows explicitly: for $y\in F(M)$, choose $b\in F(P_I)$ with $F(p)b=y$ and then $a\in T(P_I)$ with $\theta_{P_I}a=b$; naturality gives $\theta_M(T(p)a)=y$. For injectivity, if $z\in T(M)$ and $\theta_M z=0$, choose $a\in T(P_I)$ with $T(p)a=z$. Exactness gives $b\in F(P_J)$ with $F(d)b=\theta_{P_I}a$. Write $b=\theta_{P_J}c$. Naturality and injectivity of $\theta_{P_I}$ yield $a=T(d)c$, whence $z=T(p)T(d)c=0$. Thus $\theta_M$ is a bijective linear map, whose inverse is linear by applying $\theta_M$ to the addition and scalar identities. Multiplying the naturality equation by the inverse components proves their naturality, completing the natural linear isomorphism.
